The user wants UI strings for a file management app in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan usage). They need:

- s1: Button for creating a new container (容器) to organize things
- s2: Status text after creation
- s3: Dialog title for moving an item into it

Taiwan UI conventions: 「新增」 is commonly used for "create new" in Taiwan interfaces (e.g., 新增資料夾). "容器" — the user says "容器" which could mean folder-like container. Maybe use 「新增容器」. Status text after creation: 「已建立容器」or「容器已建立」. Move dialog title: 「移動項目」or「移至容器」— since the action is moving an item into the container, the title could be 「移動項目至容器」or simply 「移動項目」. Taiwan usage: 「移動」 vs 「移至」. Common in Taiwan: 「移動到…」. For dialog title when moving an item: 「移動項目」or「移至容器」.

Avoid China terms like 「新建」, 「文件夹」, 「移动...至」is fine actually. China would use 「新建」and 「窗口」etc. Taiwan uses 「新增」. So:

s1: "新增容器"
s2: "容器已建立" or "已建立容器" — Taiwan style: 「已建立容器」seems fine. Maybe "已成功建立容器" is too verbose. "容器已建立" is concise.
s3: "移動項目至容器" or "將項目移動至容器". Dialog title typically short: "移動項目".

I'll output:
{
  "s1": "新增容器",
  "s2": "已建立容器",
  "s3": "移動項目至容器"
}

Only JSON, no other text. Should I use 「」? No, plain strings.</think>{
  "s1": "新增容器",
  "s2": "已建立容器",
  "s3": "移動項目至容器"
}
